sections.title: At the Supermarket
sections.content: Shopping runs on one verb: 'necesitar', to need. It is a plain regular -ar verb, so you already know how to build it — necesito, necesitas, necesita, necesitamos. It works with a noun ('necesito pan') or with another verb ('necesito comprar pan'), exactly like 'querer' from Lesson 2. The difference is only in strength: 'quiero' is what you would like, 'necesito' is what the list says.

items.spanish: Necesitamos leche, pan, arroz y huevos.
items.english: We need milk, bread, rice and eggs.

items.spanish: Lauren toma un carrito y busca las verduras.
items.english: Lauren takes a trolley and looks for the vegetables.

items.spanish: También compramos manzanas, plátanos y naranjas.
items.english: We also buy apples, bananas and oranges.
I need two kilos of tomatoes.

sections.content: A shopping list takes no article: 'necesitamos pan y huevos', not 'necesitamos el pan y los huevos'. Put the article back when you mean particular ones — 'los tomates de la lista'.
